extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary criticism and public_oratory; educated general public interested in 19th-century letters and preaching
extracted.subtask_short: evaluating public oratory and literary prose
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the qualities that make poets, prose writers, and public preachers effective or otherwise — focusing on things like clarity, concentration, originality, physical presence, sincerity, and argumentative skill as discussed in a nineteenth-century critical essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose clarity (avoid prolixity and obscurity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose marked by "prolixity and obscurity are the most frequent characteristics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hardly a gleam of the brilliancy and richness found in conversation appears in his prose; avoid verbose, obscure writing that loses the writer's thought like "drops of water in the ground."

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful representation of conversational intellect in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: "If our author's poetry is inferior to his conversation, his prose is utterly abortive."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written work should capture the richness of the author's spoken thought and language; a gap between conversation and writing signals failure of prose/poetry to represent the mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration on a single subject (avoid digressions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Praised: "by concentrating his mind on some given object, and doing what he had to do with all his might, has accomplished much"; Fault: delighting "in nothing but episodes and digressions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained focus and working diligently on a chosen object yield substantial results; frequent episodes/digressions dissipate talent and impede accomplishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline and mastery in workmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: "He sets about his task, (whatever it may be) and goes through it with spirit and fortitude."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disciplined, dutiful approach — treating writing/argument as work to be completed resolutely — is a mark of productive genius, as opposed to being governed only by impulses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid interminable metaphysical over-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique: Coleridge "would stop to consider whether there was not more grace and beauty in a Pas de trots, and would not proceed till he had resolved this question by a chain of metaphysical reasoning without end."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive, paralyzing analysis or endless metaphysical side-questions impede finishing a composition; do not let theoretical hairsplitting prevent practical completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose and exploit one's strongest talents (avoid spreading thin)
rubrics_metrics.description: "That is best to him, which he can do best. He does not waste himself in vain aspirations and effeminate sympathies."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt mastery of every accomplishment; focus on what one can do best and avoid dissipating energies in balancing endless varieties of attainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and spectacle can drive popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation: the "preposterous rage for novelty" helps explain the success of Irving's oratory; much of the effect is "new" and spectacular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel combinations, unexpected modes, or spectacles (even at the expense of substance) attract crowds and attention — useful but potentially superficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing heterogeneous qualities (theatrical + pulpit) attracts
rubrics_metrics.description: "He has contrived to jumble these several characters together in an unheard-of and unwarranted manner, and the fascination is altogether irresistible."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining apparently incompatible modes (theatrical manner with pulpit-oratory, sacred with profane) creates striking contrasts that captivate audiences; effective for effect but may confound purists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical presence and performance matter (height, voice, action, face, eye)
rubrics_metrics.description: "To these he adds uncommon height, a graceful figure and action, a clear and powerful voice, a striking, if not a fine face, a bold and fiery spirit, and a most portentous obliquity of vision..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oratorical success depends heavily on corporeal and performative gifts; intellect alone may not launch a man into public prominence without commanding physical presence and delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provocation and attacking notable figures increases attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Irving's attacks on prominent persons (Bentham, Brougham, Canning, etc.) are noted as "rare sport" that drew attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate provocation and public onslaughts on respected figures or institutions can raise profile and draw audiences, even when not strictly relevant to doctrinal or literary merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attracting by repelling (curiosity from controversy)
rubrics_metrics.description: "He has found out the secret of attracting by repelling."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mix of attraction and offence generates curiosity: people come to see/hear partly to be affronted or to witness conflict, which can sustain popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using a platform for topical debate (blend sanctuary and forum)
rubrics_metrics.description: "He has... converted the Caledonian Chapel into a Westminster Forum or Debating Society, with the sanctity of religion added to it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transforming a traditional/sacred forum into a venue for contemporary debate is an attention-getting tactic; the sacred setting confers gravitas on modern topics but invites criticism for mixing roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writings should have intrinsic substance beyond performance
rubrics_metrics.description: On Irving's published pieces: the "ground work of his compositions is trashy and hackneyed... set off by extravagant metaphors and an affected phraseology... chat without the turn of his head and wave of his hand, his periods have nothing in them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public figure's printed work should stand on its own merits; writing that relies on oratory mannerisms fails to survive displacement from performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity, vehemence, and total engagement arrest attention
rubrics_metrics.description: "You see a man in mortal throes and agony... The integrity and vehemence of Dr. Chalmers's manner... arrests attention..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic passion and wholehearted immersion in subject-matter (even if not elegant) compel interest and lend persuasive power; theatrical polish is not a substitute for genuine commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical rigor and intricate argumentation engage intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: "He is a logician, has a theory in support of whatever he chooses to advance, and weaves the tissue of his sophistry so close and intricate, that it is difficult not to be entangled in it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully constructed argument and theoretical scaffolding draw readers/listeners into intellectual engagement; complex, sustained reasoning can be as compelling as theatrical display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity and progressive force (avoid patchy, bursty manner)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Mr. Irving wants the continuity of thought and manner which distinguishes his rival — and shines by patches and in bursts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective oratory and writing develop continuously and increase in force; mere episodic brilliance or isolated bursts of effect lack the cumulative power of sustained development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatrical affectation can amplify but risks charlatanry
rubrics_metrics.description: "Without a little charlatanry to set them off he had been nothing... He must play off his person..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate theatricality or 'charlatan' flourishes can magnify an orator's appeal, but reliance on such artifice may mask emptiness and diminish literary or intellectual reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of blending sacred and profane
rubrics_metrics.description: "He has, with an unlimited and daring licence, mixed the sacred and the profane together..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blending religious material with secular/theatrical elements creates striking contrasts that some find delightful and others confounding; consider audience expectations and potential backlash when mixing registers.
